headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when PaddleOCR outputs flow into Windsurf’s writable, networked workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can emit parsed text; Windsurf can read workspace files, use MCP, and treat file content as input. That creates a default injection path if OCR output is later opened or parsed by Windsurf. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into a Windsurf-opened file or MCP-fed prompt, injection becomes plausible.
IF Windsurf parses OCR text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled document content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any OCR text is pasted into Windsurf.
Prefix OCR outputs with a non-executable delimiter banner.
Disable MCP for the session when processing untrusted documents.
Use separate folders for raw OCR output and agent prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from OCR output to downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses broad network egress, and can send context to model proxies or MCP servers. If sensitive documents are OCRed into the shared workspace, Windsurf can transmit them onward. This is a default-path leakage risk, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are OCRed into a workspace readable by Windsurf, leakage becomes possible.
IF Windsurf forwards file contents to its model proxy or MCP server, document text can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep OCR input/output in a separate local-only directory.
Turn off network access for Windsurf during sensitive OCR jobs.
Avoid placing secrets or regulated documents in the shared workspace.
Review and redact OCR output before any upload or API call.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR itself is document-processing, but Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem. If OCR output and code edits land in the same tree, both agents can mutate shared files and git state without a documented lock, making conflicts dangerous by default.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR writes artifacts into the same workspace that Windsurf edits, concurrent file conflicts can occur.
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while OCR artifacts are being regenerated, git and filesystem state can diverge.
mitigations: Use separate worktrees for OCR artifacts and code edits.
Pause Windsurf auto-execute while OCR jobs run.
Commit or stash changes before regenerating OCR outputs.
Restrict Windsurf to read-only access on the OCR output directory.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspace writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text that Windsurf may treat as authoritative input for code or shell actions. Windsurf’s tool-use loop and shell/network capabilities mean a bad OCR parse can cascade into incorrect edits or commands. Because no verification layer is documented, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses OCR output as source text for edits or commands, extraction errors can propagate.
IF the OCR text contains malformed instructions or code blocks, Windsurf may act on them without verification.
mitigations: Require human review of OCR output before any action-taking.
Compare OCR text against the source document for critical fields.
Disable command auto-execute for workflows using OCR output.
Use a checksum or diff step between OCR output and downstream edits.
requires-engineering: add structured validation for OCR-derived inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR is open-source and document-processing, while Windsurf is closed-source, handles model provider keys, and can send workspace content to external model proxies. If regulated documents are OCRed and then processed by Windsurf, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The pair’s compliance posture is therefore mismatched in default use.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through Windsurf after OCR, external retention or residency rules may apply.
IF the workspace contains EU PII or PHI and Windsurf sends it to a model proxy, compliance obligations can be breached.
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of Windsurf sessions.
Confirm vendor DPA and retention terms before processing sensitive data.
Use local-only OCR and local-only downstream review for regulated files.
Redact personal data before passing OCR text onward.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated content.
